gap: No result ChatGPT got prices a whole-home-sized (about 24-30 kWh, 240 V, automatic switchover) battery from today's store pages. At equipment cost before installation, the Anker SOLIX E10 with 24.6 kWh and Power Dock is $13,798 ($561/kWh). The FranklinWH 2× aPower 2 + aGate (30 kWh) is $20,578 ($686/kWh). Six Enphase IQ Battery 5P units plus IQ System Controller 3 (30 kWh) come to $23,430 ($781/kWh). The EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X 12 kWh + Smart Home Panel 3 is $10,899 ($887/kWh). Tesla's Powerwall 3 has only an installed average, $998/kWh (EnergySage).
standout_why: I compared five pages. solutionenergy.com/batteries/without-solar and solarpanelx.com give Tesla and FranklinWH only as EnergySage installed averages ($967/kWh and $1,232/kWh), and price the E10 only as one 6 kWh battery with Power Dock ($5,799). outagereadyhq.com prices portable units and their transfer kits (DELTA Pro 3, F3800 Plus, Apex 300, Jackery 5000 Plus, DELTA Pro Ultra) as of Oct 24 to Nov 10. None of them gives FranklinWH or Enphase equipment prices, a 24-30 kWh whole-home configuration priced from a store today, or a per-kWh comparison across both kinds of system. energysavvyhomes.com could not be read (TLS error), and stormwatts.com was not read.
decides: ChatGPT's answer suggests two Powerwall 3s or two aPower 2s for about 27-30 kWh, at $22,000-$35,000 installed. Store prices today show the shopper can buy whole-home-sized equipment for 30 kWh for $20,578 (FranklinWH, installer still needed) or 24.6 kWh with automatic switchover for $13,798 (Anker SOLIX E10, which Dealectric lists). That puts the E10 ahead on equipment cost per kWh among systems with automatic whole-home switchover. Portable 240 V units (Apex 300 kit $579/kWh) are cheaper per kWh, but at 3.84 kW they cannot carry a whole house with central AC. Installation is extra on every equipment price, and Powerwall 3 has no public equipment price, so the Tesla comparison is installed against equipment-only.
